newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel urges EU not to pressure Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel urges EU not to pressure Netanyahu.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Monday the European Union should not put political or economic pressure on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to patch up the crumbling peace with the Palestinians.

But Kinkel denied an Israeli press report that Bonn was opposed to the European Union sending its own mission to the Middle East to make sure it would not be left out of peace talks between Israelis and Palestinians.

"The EU should not put Netanyahu under pressure," Kinkel said in an interview with WDR German radio. "Europe should be prepared to help when the Israelis and Palestinians want them to...the Europeans should not overestimate their importance."

Kinkel said he expected the Israelis to budge eventually on a long-delayed Israeli troop pullback from the West Bank city of Hebron and on the opening of an archaelogical tunnel in Jerusalem that sparked recent Israeli-Arab violence.
Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring left for the Middle East on Sunday following an EU summit in Dublin at the weekend.
Irish officials say he has since met Netanyahu, U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat.
France -- anxious to retain its historic presence in the region and traditionally wary of U.S. foreign policy engagements -- was the chief mover behind sending the mission.
